Alex — thanks for the clear list. Quick summary up front, followed by specifics and attachments:

Summary (short):
- Hosted default retention for audit/access logs: 90 days by default; configurable up to 7 years for Dedicated/Private.
- Residency metadata: Yes — each log line includes region, availability-zone, and serving model shard id when applicable.
- Export: We support scheduled exports to S3 (Parquet or CSV) and ad-hoc exports via the Console or the /exports API.
- Deletion proof: We can provide an export of the deletion audit (deletion_time, operator, request_id) plus a signed attestation PDF for auditor use.

Details and attachments: I've attached the export instructions PDF (redwood_audit_export_instructions.pdf) that walks through the Console schedule and the exports API. A few additional notes below:

Retention by deployment type:
- Hosted (default): 90 days. This is the default retention window for audit/access logs stored in our managed telemetry cluster.
- Dedicated: Customers can request retention beyond 90 days up to 7 years via their reserved capacity contract; we surface this in the Dedicated tenancy settings.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): Retention is customer-controlled; Redwood only enforces retention if we're operating the storage layer.

Export capabilities:
- Formats: Parquet (recommended for analytics), CSV (quick look), and NDJSON for event-stream tooling.
- Scheduling: Daily or hourly exports; you can pick a region-level export job to ensure entries include residency fields.
- Delivery: S3 push (AWS cross-account role) or secure HTTPS pull with signed URLs.
- Schema: See s3_export_schema.csv included here for the field list (timestamp, event_type, principal_id, region, az, model_shard, request_id, kv_cache_id, request_payload_ref).

Deletion and auditor evidence:
- Deletion flow: When a retention policy expires or a targeted deletion request is submitted, the row-level entries are removed from the primary telemetry index and the event is recorded to an immutable deletion journal (retains only metadata: request_id, deletion_time, operator_id, scope).
- Proof artifact: We provide a signed deletion-report (PDF) and the journal export containing request_id + checksum of removed export files. For Dedicated/Private customers we can also run on-prem agents that produce local deletion receipts.

Adding a few infra specifics from the operations side so your auditors have the technical details:

- Export window guarantees: Exports are generated from our cold-store snapshot. For hosted customers we guarantee export completeness for any 90-day sliding window; for Dedicated we support backfills up to the configured retention.
- Residency field behavior: region/az fields are populated at write time. If a request is served from a fallback model in another region (policy routing), the entry includes both origin_region and serve_region fields.
- Export integrity: Each export file contains a SHA256 manifest file. When a scheduled S3 push completes we write a manifest object to the destination bucket with file checksums and a job_id.
- Deletion mechanics for exports: Exports already handed off to customer S3 are the customer's copy — Redwood cannot delete those. For managed copies we prune files according to retention and write a tombstone entry to the deletion journal. The signed deletion-report references the manifest job_id(s) that were removed.
- Minimal PII guidance: The export schema includes principal_id (internal user id). If you require pseudonymization, we offer a pseudonymization transform step during export (hashing + salt) — requestable via export profile.

I've attached s3_export_schema.csv as a quick reference and included a short example of the S3 role policy we recommend in the PDF.
